newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber ends down slightly after wide swings.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber ends down slightly after wide swings.

text.p: CME lumber futures showed a very wide price range that included a brief limit loss of $10.00 per tbf in July before closing a little lower.
Lumber closed $4.50 per tbf lower to unchanged with July off $1.90 at $372.00, after plunging the daily limit to $363.90, and September off $1.00 at $354.80 per tbf.

Futures ranged mixed as short-covering on mill closings and labor concerns lent support while views were mixed on the U.S. housing starts report. Lower starts prompted commission house selling but a slightly higher permit number also lent support at times, traders said.

The Commerce Department reported May housing starts down 4.8 percent to 1.397 million unit annual rate. This compared with a Reuters survey which averaged 1.47 million units in a range of 1.42 to 1.50 million.

Starts were down for a third consecutive month for the first time since early 1995. However, economists said the housing sector is still at healthy levels and even though the May number was down it did not indicate declines in the foreseeable future.
